subject.title: macOS update can leave manual-update loop and stale node host causing Gateway restart storm

question: For macOS managed updates, should same-version package refresh and repeated updater workers short-circuit before managed Gateway stop/restart, and should stale launchd cleanup explicitly include the `ai.openclaw.manualupdate.<date>.<epoch>` family?
rationale: Current behavior intentionally refreshes same-version package installs and current cleanup intentionally narrows label matching; changing either affects update semantics and launchd safety, so automation should not pick the policy alone.

options.title: Keep Open And Design One Lifecycle Fix
options.body: Treat issue 87928 as canonical, define the accepted no-op/dedupe and label cleanup contract, then require real macOS launchd proof before closure.

options.title: Split Into Narrow Canonical Items
options.body: Move `manualupdate` detection, no-op update policy, launchd rebootstrap proof, and node-host restart into separate owner-approved issues while keeping this open until every part is linked.

options.title: Preserve Current Refresh Semantics
options.body: If maintainers want same-version refresh to keep stopping/restarting services, document that policy and only fix stale updater diagnostics/recovery.

recommendation.title: Keep Open And Design One Lifecycle Fix
recommendation.body: Treat issue 87928 as canonical, define the accepted no-op/dedupe and label cleanup contract, then require real macOS launchd proof before closure.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent package service-state and macOS update lifecycle history plus adjacent maintainer comments make this the best available owner for the behavior decision.
